info.title: QbAutopost API v2
info.description:
The dashboard surface under `/api/v2` (docs/saved-requests-dashboard-v2.md). Paths are the v1 ones, relative to the prefix. Every route here uses the same scope as its v1 twin; `x-required-scope` on each operation is the scope the middleware actually enforces.

This document is **hand-authored** (`src/QbAutopost.Api/wwwroot/openapi-v2.json`) and kept honest by `OpenApiV2DriftTests`, which compares it with the application's own `/api/v2` route table. The v1 document at `/api/v1/openapi.json` is unchanged.

This document is served only when `Api:Reference:Enabled` is true, and needs the `health:read` scope.

get.summary: Saved-requests database: reachability, schema state and check latency.
get.description: Looks at the database now. Never includes the connection string. With `Database:ConnectionString` empty the feature is off and this answers 503 with reason `not-configured`; the rest of the API is unaffected. Either `requests:read` (any dashboard user, for the status light) or `health:read` satisfies it.

200.description: The database answered and its schema is current.

503.description: Not configured, unreachable, or the schema is out of date; `reason` says which.

get.summary: The cached QuickBooks account, vendor and customer names.
get.description: Read from `qb-lists.json`, so it answers while QuickBooks is shut down and never queues behind a post. A `syncedUtc` of `null` with empty lists means the sync has not run yet; it is not an error. Needs `lists:read`, which every dashboard role holds; an API key holding `qb:read` satisfies it too.

200.description: The names as the last sync left them.

get.description: Served only when `Api:Reference:Enabled` is true, under the same rules as `/api/v1/openapi.json`; otherwise the route is not mapped at all and the answer is 404. There is no v2 reference page.

post.summary: Sign in with email and password.
post.description: Answers an access token (JWT, HS256, `Auth:Jwt:AccessTokenMinutes`) and sets the refresh cookie `qbautopost_refresh` (`HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/api/v2/auth`, `Auth:Jwt:RefreshTokenDays`). The v2 cookie path is `/api/v2/auth`, so v1 and v2 sessions never see each other's cookie. An unknown email, a wrong password and a disabled account all answer the same `401 invalid-credentials`. `Auth:Lockout:MaxFailedAttempts` wrong passwords lock the account for `Auth:Lockout:LockoutMinutes` (`423 locked-out`). Failed sign-ins are also braked per address and per email by `Api:RateLimits:FailedAuthPerMinute` (`429`). Every failure is recorded in `user_audit`. `503 auth-not-configured` when `Auth:Jwt:SigningKey` is missing; `503 database-unavailable` when the database is not ready.

200.description: Signed in. The refresh cookie is set.

401.description: Wrong credentials: unknown email, wrong password or disabled account. One answer for all three (`invalid-credentials`).

423.description: `locked-out`: too many wrong passwords; `Retry-After` says for how long.

post.summary: Exchange the refresh cookie for a new access token and a new refresh cookie.
post.description: Takes no body and no header credential: only the `qbautopost_refresh` cookie, which v2 sets and clears with `Path=/api/v2/auth`. The presented token is revoked and its successor set. **Reuse grace (v2 only):** a token that was already revoked is accepted once more, and a second successor issued in its family (both successors stay valid), when all of these hold: (a) it was revoked by rotation and its family is not revoked; (b) that was at most `Auth:Jwt:RefreshReuseGraceSeconds` ago (default 30); (c) its successor is neither rotated nor revoked; (d) the caller's address equals the address the successor was issued to (an unknown address gets no grace); (e) no grace was given for it before. Otherwise presenting a revoked token revokes its whole family (a theft signal), answers `401` and is recorded in `user_audit` as `refresh-reuse` with `{ familyId }`; a missing, unknown or expired token also answers `401`, and the cookie is then cleared. v1 refresh has no grace.

200.description: A new access token; the refresh cookie is replaced.

401.description: `invalid-refresh-token`: missing, unknown, expired or revoked. The cookie is cleared.

post.summary: Sign out: revoke the current refresh token and clear the cookie.
post.description: Revokes the refresh token in the `qbautopost_refresh` cookie (that token only, none of the caller's others), and always clears the cookie. Allowed while a password change is pending.

get.summary: The signed-in user, their role and its scopes.
get.description: Allowed while a password change is pending, so the dashboard can tell the user to change it.

post.description: Needs the current password. The new one needs `Auth:Password:MinLength` characters (12) and nothing else (`400 invalid-password`). A wrong current password answers `400 current-password-incorrect` and counts toward lockout. On success the security stamp rotates (older access tokens stop working), `mustChangePassword` is cleared, every other refresh token of the user is revoked, and a new access token is returned; the current refresh cookie stays valid.

200.description: Changed. Use the access token in this answer from now on.

423.description: `locked-out`: too many wrong passwords; `Retry-After` says for how long.

post.description: The answer is `201` with the user and `temporaryPassword` (16 characters, shown once, never stored in plain text, `Cache-Control: no-store`). patch.summary: Change a user's display name, role or disabled flag.
patch.description: Needs `If-Match`. A role change replaces the old role in one save, so the user never holds zero or two roles. Changing the role or disabling the user rotates their security stamp (so their access tokens stop at once, not after the 30 s gate cache) and revokes all their refresh tokens; both are recorded in `user_audit` (`role-changed`, `disabled`, `enabled`). Demoting or disabling the only enabled admin answers `409 last-admin`, also when two admins do it to each other at the same moment (the admins are row-locked in one transaction). An admin cannot disable themselves (`409 cannot-disable-self`).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The user's id.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The user's ETag from `GET /users/{id}` (Identity's concurrency stamp, in quotes). Missing answers `428 precondition-required`, a stale one `412 edited-by-someone-else`. Any failed sign-in of that user also changes it, so a `412` may only mean "reload".

ETag.description: The user's ETag, to send back in `If-Match`.

post.description: Sets `mustChangePassword`, rotates the security stamp and revokes all the user's refresh tokens, so their sessions end at once. The new password is in the answer once (`Cache-Control: no-store`). Recorded as `password-reset`.

post.summary: Save a validate-and-post body for a person to review and post.
post.description: Saved-requests §6.1. The body is exactly the validate-and-post body; nothing is posted. Over `Api:MaxRequestBodyBytes` answers `413` and anything that is not one JSON object `400 not-a-json-object`; neither is stored. Every JSON object is stored, its original body byte for byte, even when it cannot be read (`needsAttention: true`, the JSON path in `validation.errors`) or when validation refuses it (`dryRun`, `allowModelAccounts`, control-total mismatch, too many rows) or holds rows. When validation cannot run (rules file missing, lists unreadable) the snapshot is `unavailable` and the save still succeeds. A request that looks like another one is flagged (`duplicate`), never refused. `createdBy` and `updatedBy` come from the caller, never the body. Treat any `201` as success. v2 (dashboard v2 §5, §7.1): rows without an `externalId` get `row-<n>` in version 1, while `GET …/original` keeps the exact bytes; `email` and `pushId` are read from the body as received; the canonical hash ignores `email`, `pushId` and `post: true`. Repeats are checked in order: `Idempotency-Key` (its rules alone when it matches), then `pushId`.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Honoured per source (§10.1), by the store rather than the replay file: the same key and body answer `200` with the existing record and save nothing; the same key with a different body answers `409 idempotency-key-reused`. At most 128 characters.

200.description: Nothing was saved; the existing record. Either the same `Idempotency-Key` and body were saved before, or (no key matched) the same `pushId` with the same body.

Idempotency-Replayed.description: `true`: the existing record, nothing was saved.

400.description: `not-a-json-object`: the body is not one JSON object (or not UTF-8); nothing was saved. `invalid-request`: the `Idempotency-Key` is too long.

409.description: `idempotency-key-reused`: this source used the key for a different body. `push-id-reused`: the `pushId` is held by another request with a different body (`savedRequestId`, `publicRef` name it). Nothing was saved.

413.description: The body is over `Api:MaxRequestBodyBytes`; nothing was saved.

503.description: `database-unavailable`: the database is not ready (`Retry-After: 30`); nothing was read or changed.

get.summary: List saved requests, filtered and paged.
get.description: Saved-requests §6.5 with dashboard v2 §9.2: v1's parameters plus `receivedFrom`, `receivedTo`, `emailFrom`, `reference`, `minTotal`, `maxTotal`, `hasErrors` the sorts `received`, `total` and `rows`, and (dashboard-api-m12 §5) `postedFrom`, `postedTo`, `tz` and the sort `posted`, all combined with AND. `needsAttention`, `hasErrors` and the rows' flags use the v2 judgement (§5.3). Every value is checked: an unknown `status` or `sort`, a flag that is not `true`/`false`, a date that is neither `yyyy-MM-dd` nor an instant with an offset, an unknown `tz`, a total that is not an invariant decimal, `minTotal` above `maxTotal`, or a page outside its range answers `400 invalid-request`.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Repeatable. Only these statuses.

parameters.name: needsAttention
parameters.description: Only requests that do (`true`) or do not (`false`) need attention under the v2 rule (§5.3).

parameters.name: duplicate
parameters.description: Only flagged (`true`) or unflagged (`false`) requests.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text in the reference, the public reference, a payee or memo inside the payload, or the email subject. When it is 1 to 32 hex digits (dashes ignored) it also matches the start of the `pushId`.

parameters.name: createdFrom
parameters.description: Created on or after this date. Inclusive: from the start of the day. A plain date is a UTC day, or with `tz` a local day in that zone; an ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`2026-10-27T00:00:00+05:30`, write `+` as `%2B`) is used as is and ignores `tz`.

schema.description: `yyyy-MM-dd` or an ISO 8601 instant with an offset.

parameters.name: createdTo
parameters.description: Created on or before this date. A date covers the whole day; an instant is exclusive. A plain date is a UTC day, or with `tz` a local day in that zone; an ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`2026-10-27T00:00:00+05:30`, write `+` as `%2B`) is used as is and ignores `tz`.

schema.description: `yyyy-MM-dd` or an ISO 8601 instant with an offset.

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: `api-client:<clientId>` or `user:<userId>`.

parameters.name: receivedFrom
parameters.description: Received on or after this date: the email's `receivedUtc`, else the save time. Inclusive: from the start of the day. A plain date is a UTC day, or with `tz` a local day in that zone; an ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`2026-10-27T00:00:00+05:30`, write `+` as `%2B`) is used as is and ignores `tz`.

schema.description: `yyyy-MM-dd` or an ISO 8601 instant with an offset.

parameters.name: receivedTo
parameters.description: Received on or before this date, as `receivedFrom`. A date covers the whole day; an instant is exclusive. A plain date is a UTC day, or with `tz` a local day in that zone; an ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`2026-10-27T00:00:00+05:30`, write `+` as `%2B`) is used as is and ignores `tz`.

schema.description: `yyyy-MM-dd` or an ISO 8601 instant with an offset.

parameters.name: postedFrom
parameters.description: Posted on or after this day or instant: the list's `postSummary.postedUtc` (the latest posted or partial attempt's finish, or the resolve time of a request resolved to posted). A request with no post never matches when `postedFrom` or `postedTo` is sent. A plain date is a UTC day, or with `tz` a local day in that zone; an ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`2026-10-27T00:00:00+05:30`, write `+` as `%2B`) is used as is and ignores `tz`.

schema.description: `yyyy-MM-dd` or an ISO 8601 instant with an offset.

parameters.name: postedTo
parameters.description: Posted on or before this day (the whole day), or before this instant (exclusive), as `postedFrom`. A plain date is a UTC day, or with `tz` a local day in that zone; an ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`2026-10-27T00:00:00+05:30`, write `+` as `%2B`) is used as is and ignores `tz`.

schema.description: `yyyy-MM-dd` or an ISO 8601 instant with an offset.

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: An IANA time zone id (`Asia/Kolkata`). Makes a plain date in `createdFrom`, `createdTo`, `receivedFrom`, `receivedTo`, `postedFrom` and `postedTo` a local day in this zone. Without it a plain date is a UTC day, as before. An unknown id answers `400 invalid-request`.

parameters.name: emailFrom
parameters.description: Case-insensitive text in the email's `from`.

parameters.name: reference
parameters.description: Exactly this reference.

parameters.name: minTotal
parameters.description: `controlTotal` at least this (invariant decimal, e.g. `1250.00`). A request without a total is left out when `minTotal` or `maxTotal` is given.

parameters.name: maxTotal
parameters.description: `controlTotal` at most this, as `minTotal`. Below `minTotal` answers `400`.

parameters.name: hasErrors
parameters.description: `true`: requests with a problem (`validationSummary.problemCount` above 0) or that need attention; `false`: the others.

parameters.name: sort
parameters.description: Default `-created`; a leading `-` is descending. `received` is the email's received time, else the save time; `total` is `controlTotal` (no total last); `rows` is `transactionCount`. Ties are broken by id. `posted` is `postSummary.postedUtc`; requests without a post sort last in both directions, then by id descending.

parameters.name: page
parameters.description: 1 or more. Default 1.

parameters.name: pageSize
parameters.description: 1 to `SavedRequests:MaxListPageSize` (100). Default 25.

get.description: Dashboard v2 §9.3. `byStatus` names every status, zero included. Each flag is counted among `pending` requests and among `all`, on the v2 judgement (§5.3); `hasErrors` is a problem count above 0 or needing attention.

get.summary: One saved request: latest payload, flags, validation snapshot and last attempt.
get.description: Saved-requests §6.2 with dashboard v2 §9.1 and §10 (4.1, 4.3, 4.9). The `ETag` is the row version, to send as `If-Match` on an edit or a post. `needsAttention` and `validation` are the v2 judgement. `readErrors` lists the metadata errors (e.g. `$.pushId: not a UUID`) first, then the read errors of the current version, then its `post` errors. `allowedActions` follows the status and the caller's scopes; an API key never gets an action. Actors are `{ id, name, email }` for a user and `{ id, name }` for an API client (`api-client:<id>`).

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else, including `0`, a sign or more than 18 digits, answers `404`.

put.summary: Replace the payload of a pending saved request; the old payload stays as an earlier version.
put.description: Saved-requests §6.3, §8. The body is `{ "payload": { ...the full validate-and-post body... }, "note": "..." }`: a full payload, not a patch. `If-Match` is required. A payload that differs from the current one becomes version n+1 with its change list (numbers are compared as decimals, so `184.3` and `184.30` are equal), validation and the duplicate rules run again, and an `edited` event is written. An identical payload answers `200` and writes nothing. An unreadable payload is stored and flagged like a save. The API never recalculates `controlTotal`: change it together with an amount, or validation reports the mismatch. Only a `pending` request can be edited. **v2 (§7, §7.1):** the payload is hashed and diffed by the v2 rules (top-level `email` and `pushId` are ignored, and a row's missing `post` equals `true`, so turning a row off is `replace $.transactions[i].post true → false`); a payload that differs only there answers `200` unchanged. A row without an `externalId` gets `edit<v>-<n>` (`v` the new version number, `n` its 1-based position). The edit never changes `email` or `pushId`. Both snapshots are refreshed; the reply shows the v2 one, which honours `post: false`.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else answers `404`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The row version from the last `GET` (its `ETag`), in quotes.

note.description: Why it was changed; kept with the version.

200.description: The saved request after the edit (or unchanged, when the payload was identical), as the v2 detail (the same shape as `GET /api/v2/saved-requests/{id}`).

400.description: `not-a-json-object`: the body is not an object with a `payload` object (or not UTF-8); nothing was stored. `invalid-request`: `note` is not text.

409.description: `not-editable`: the request is not `pending`; the detail names its status. Nothing was changed.

412.description: `edited-by-someone-else`: the `If-Match` row version is not the current one. The body carries the current `rowVersion`, `updatedUtc` and `updatedBy` (`{ id, name }`), so the dashboard can say who changed it and when. Nothing was changed.

413.description: The body is over `Api:MaxRequestBodyBytes`; nothing was stored.

post.summary: Re-run validation and the duplicate rules for the current version and store the new snapshot.
post.description: Saved-requests §6.4. Takes no body. Rules, lists and the ledger change after a snapshot was taken, so this refreshes it (`validation.validatedUtc` moves) and writes a `validated` event. It bumps the row version, so an `ETag` held before goes stale. The snapshot is advisory: Post always validates again. Only a `pending` request can be validated. **v2 (§6.4):** both snapshots are refreshed; the reply shows the v2 one, which sets the rows marked `post: false` aside.

parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else answers `404`.

200.description: The saved request with its refreshed snapshot, as the v2 detail (the same shape as `GET /api/v2/saved-requests/{id}`).

ETag.description: The new row version, in quotes.

409.description: `not-editable`: the request is not `pending`; the detail names its status. Nothing was changed.

412.description: `edited-by-someone-else`: the request was edited between this validation's read and its write. The body carries the current `rowVersion`, `updatedUtc` and `updatedBy` (`{ id, name }`), so the dashboard can say who changed it and when. Nothing was validated.

post.summary: Settle an unknown or partial post (admin only).
post.description: Saved-requests §10.6. After a person has checked QuickBooks (the attempt's `ledgerBatch`, from `GET /saved-requests/{id}/attempts/{attemptId}`, lists the batch and the transaction ids to look up). `posted` moves the request to `posted` and copies the attempt's `postId`; `not-posted` moves it to `pending`. Only `unknown` can go either way; `partial` can only be `posted` (accepted as is): to post the remaining rows, create a new saved request. The note is required, 1 to 500 characters after trimming; the resolver and the note are stored on the attempt and in a `resolved` event. Nothing is sent to QuickBooks. `If-Match` is optional; when sent, it must be the current row version.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else answers `404`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The row version from the last `GET`, in quotes. Optional.

outcome.description: What a person found in QuickBooks.

200.description: The request, `posted` or `pending`, as the v2 detail (the same shape as `GET /api/v2/saved-requests/{id}`).

ETag.description: The new row version, in quotes.

400.description: `invalid-request`: the body is not an object with a valid `outcome` and a note of 1 to 500 characters. Nothing was changed.

409.description: `not-resolvable`: the request is not `unknown` or `partial`, or it is `partial` and the outcome is `not-posted`; the detail names its status. Nothing was changed.

412.description: `edited-by-someone-else`: the `If-Match` row version is not the current one. The body carries the current `rowVersion`, `updatedUtc` and `updatedBy` (`{ id, name }`), so the dashboard can say who changed it and when. Nothing was changed.

post.summary: Post the current version through validate-and-post, and record the attempt.
post.description: Saved-requests §7.2, §9, §10.2-§10.6. The request is claimed (pending to posting, with an `in-progress` attempt) and the claim is committed before anything is sent, so of two people pressing Post exactly one posts and the other is answered `409 already-posting`. The current version is then posted by validate-and-post's own engine and the answer is **validate-and-post's status code and body**, unchanged, plus `savedRequestId`, `attemptId` and `savedRequestStatus` (the request's status after the attempt). Every ending is recorded on the attempt with its HTTP status, post id, counts and the body returned. Nothing is retried automatically. The post runs to the end even if the caller disconnects: read `GET /saved-requests/{id}` until it is no longer `posting`. A request flagged as a possible duplicate needs `{ "confirmDuplicate": true }`; the confirming user and time are stored. Only `pending` requests can be posted. v2 (dashboard v2 §6.2): a row marked `post: false` is never sent to QuickBooks; it still counts toward `controlTotal` (which is never recalculated), is listed under `skipped` with `reason: "not-to-post"` and counted in `counts.skipped`, and never makes a post `partial` or `failed`. When every row is `post: false` the answer is `400 nothing-to-post` and nothing is claimed.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The numeric id (`123`) or the public reference (`SR-000123`). Anything else answers `404`.

parameters.name: If-Match
parameters.description: The request's ETag from `GET /saved-requests/{id}`. When sent and stale the answer is `412` and nothing is claimed, so a person never posts a version they have not seen.

confirmDuplicate.description: Required (`true`) to post a request flagged as a possible duplicate (§9). G4 still runs inside the post.

200.description: validate-and-post's `200`: posted (request `posted`), `partial` (request `partial`, locked), or `failed`. A `failed` post with a row held for `quickbooks-no-response` or `quickbooks-busy` was sent and not confirmed, so the request goes to `unknown`, locked until an admin resolves it; any other `failed` returns it to `pending`. The saved route adds `savedRequestId`, `attemptId` and `savedRequestStatus` (the request's status after the attempt, kebab-case). If the result could not be recorded, `savedRequestStatus` is `posting` and the result is in the evidence file.

400.description: validate-and-post's `400` (control total, too many rows, `dryRun`, `allowModelAccounts`, ...), or the current version could not be bound, including a row whose `post` is not `true` or `false` (`$.transactions[i].post: must be true or false`): then `errors` names each JSON path. Recorded as `refused`; the request is `pending` again. The saved route adds `savedRequestId`, `attemptId` and `savedRequestStatus` (the request's status after the attempt, kebab-case). Or `nothing-to-post` (problem `type`): every row is marked `post: false`, so nothing would be sent; this is checked before the claim, so no attempt is made, the request stays `pending` and the body has none of the saved route's fields.

409.description: `already-posting` (with the running `attemptId`, `startedBy` and `startedUtc`), `already-posted` (with the `postId`, and the `attemptId`, `startedBy` and `startedUtc` of the attempt that posted it; all three are null when an admin settled the request by resolve), `not-postable` (partial, unknown or discarded; `savedRequestStatus` names it) or `duplicate-unconfirmed` (`duplicate: { of, status, reasons }`): nothing was claimed or sent. Or validate-and-post's busy `409` with `Retry-After`: recorded as `busy`, the request is `pending` again. The saved route adds `savedRequestId`, `attemptId` and `savedRequestStatus` (the request's status after the attempt, kebab-case).

412.description: `edited-by-someone-else`: `If-Match` is not the current row version, or the request changed between the duplicate check and the claim (the claim is made at the row version the check read). The body carries the current `rowVersion`, `updatedUtc` and `updatedBy`. Nothing was claimed or sent.

413.description: The body is over `Api:MaxRequestBodyBytes`; nothing was claimed.

422.description: validate-and-post's `422`: at least one row would be held, so none was sent. Recorded as `held`; the request is `pending` again. The saved route adds `savedRequestId`, `attemptId` and `savedRequestStatus` (the request's status after the attempt, kebab-case).

500.description: `post-not-started`: the engine failed before the post was started; nothing was sent and the request is `pending` again (attempt `error`). Or `post-outcome-unknown`: it failed after the post was started, QuickBooks may have it, and the request is `unknown`, locked until an admin resolves it. The saved route adds `savedRequestId`, `attemptId` and `savedRequestStatus` (the request's status after the attempt, kebab-case).

503.description: validate-and-post's `503` (backup too old, QuickBooks unreachable: a `SyncPostResult` body) or the rules file is missing (problem details): nothing was sent, recorded as `unavailable`, the request is `pending` again. The saved route adds `savedRequestId`, `attemptId` and `savedRequestStatus` (the request's status after the attempt, kebab-case). Or `database-unavailable` (`Retry-After: 30`): nothing was read, claimed or sent.

get.description: Dashboard-api-m12 §4. `counts` and `previous` equal the audit feed's `total` for `received`, `posted`, `post-failed` and `discarded` over the same range (`post-failed` includes `partial`). `posted` is money that reached QuickBooks: the entries and the sum of `posted[].amount` in the stored result of each attempt that finished `posted` or `partial` in the range; amounts are JSON numbers with two decimals. `timeToPost` measures minutes from received to posted for each request whose post time is in the range (nearest rank, rounded down) and is `null` when there is none. `series` has one entry per local day (or Monday-started week) in `tz` overlapping the range, empty ones included, clipped to the range, so it sums to `counts`. parameters.name: from

apiKeyAuth.name: X-Api-Key
apiKeyAuth.description: `X-Api-Key: <key>` — the header this build reads, and the one every operation is secured with here. Each key belongs to one caller in `clients.json` and carries only the scopes that caller was given; `x-required-scope` on every operation names the one it needs.

bearerAuth.description: `Authorization: Bearer <access token>`: a dashboard user's JWT (saved-requests §11.3), not an API key. An API key still travels only in `X-Api-Key` (Q-67); sending both headers answers `400 ambiguous-credentials`.

BadRequest.description: Malformed or self-inconsistent request. Nothing was posted.

Unauthorized.description: No key, or a key no caller holds.

Forbidden.description: The key is known but lacks the scope this operation needs.

Conflict.description: A state conflict, or an `Idempotency-Key` replayed with a different body.

TooManyRequests.description: Rate limited; `Retry-After` says for how long.

Unavailable.description: QuickBooks or Hermes is unreachable or busy, or the app is not ready.

name.description: The user's display name, the API client's name, or the id when nobody can name it.

index.description: The index in the new version for an added or replaced row, in the previous version for a removed one.

old.description: The value before, as stored; null when there is none.

new.description: The value after, as stored; null when there is none.

role.description: `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`; empty when the account holds no role, or more than one (Q-87).

lockedOutUntilUtc.description: Set only while a lockout is still running.

role.description: `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`; empty when the account holds no role, or more than one (Q-87).

lockedOutUntilUtc.description: Set only while a lockout is still running.

temporaryPassword.description: 16 characters from an unambiguous alphabet. Shown once; hand it over and it is gone.

UserStatus.description: Exactly one holds, evaluated in this order: `disabled`; `locked` (not disabled, and the lockout has not ended); `must-change-password`; `active`.

role.description: `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`; empty when the account holds no role, or more than one (Q-87).

lockedOutUntilUtc.description: Set only while a lockout is still running.

role.description: `admin`, `editor` or `viewer`; empty when the account holds no role, or more than one (Q-87), and it then has no scopes.

mustChangePassword.description: While true every route except `me`, `change-password` and `logout` answers `403 password-change-required`.

Problem.description: RFC 7807 problem details. `requestId` is the same id as the `X-Request-Id` header and every log line of that request.

errors.description: Present when the failure is per item.

SyncPostRequest.description: `DirectRequest` minus `dryRun` (validate-and-post §4). The rows are identical, so a caller can move between the two posting routes without rewriting one.

reference.description: The caller's own name for this post; it names the ledger row `api-<reference>`.

controlTotal.description: Required here. The caller's own sum over every submitted row: checked to the cent, never corrected. A mismatch refuses the whole request and no amount is adjusted to make it agree.

dryRun.description: NOT A FIELD OF THIS ROUTE. Sending any value, `false` included, is refused with 400 `dry-run-not-supported` — a caller who asks for a dry run and is answered `posted` would have moved money they believed they were only checking. Use `POST /api/v1/quickbooks/transactions/validate` to check a batch without sending it.

allowModelAccounts.description: NOT IMPLEMENTED, as on the direct path (T-915): tiers 3-4 never run here, so the flag would silently do nothing. Sending it is refused with 400. Give each row a `lineAccount`, or add a rule for its last four (Q-51).

SyncPostResult.description: What landed in QuickBooks (validate-and-post §6.1). There is no `batchId`, `dryRun` or `isRunning`: this route has no batch to poll and no mode to choose.

postId.description: Names the ledger row, for `POST /api/v1/batches/{id}/undo`. It is NOT a polling resource — no `GET` accepts it. It contains `#`, which must be sent percent-encoded as `%23`.

status.description: `posted` on the ordinary path: a held row is a 422 before anything is sent. It can still read `partial` or `failed` if a gate that runs after the SDK was touched (G4's live half, G5) refused a row — a caller whose money half-moved is told, not reassured.

skipped.description: Rows a skip rule or G4 excluded, plus (post by id in v2) rows marked `post: false`; why `posted` can be below `submitted` on a clean post.

externalId.description: The caller's own key, echoed so a batch can be reconciled against their records.

txnId.description: QuickBooks' own id for the transaction.

held.description: Empty on the ordinary path; a held row is a 422 before anything is sent.

skipped.description: Rows a skip rule or G4 excluded, and (post by id in v2) every row marked `post: false`, with `reason: "not-to-post"`.

SavedPostFields.description: What post by id adds to validate-and-post's body or problem (saved-requests §7.2). All three are present whenever an attempt was made. They are absent on 404, 412 and `database-unavailable`; of the 409s that claim nothing, `already-posting` carries `attemptId` (the running attempt) with `SavedPostConflictFields`, and `not-postable` only `savedRequestStatus`. `400 nothing-to-post` carries none of them.

savedRequestStatus.description: The request's status after the attempt. Named apart from `status`, which stays validate-and-post's (Q-90). `posting` means the result could not be recorded and is in the evidence file.

SavedPostConflictFields.description: Dashboard v2 §10 item 4.4: what the v2 `already-posting` and `already-posted` add. On `already-posted` the attempt fields are null when the request was settled by resolve.

attemptId.description: The running attempt (`already-posting`) or the attempt that posted the request (`already-posted`).

startedBy.description: Who started that attempt: `{ id, name }`.

postId.description: `already-posted` only: the post that is in QuickBooks.

SyncPostProblem.description: The 422 of validate-and-post §6.2: RFC 7807, with every finding in `validation` — not the first, because one held row refuses the whole request and a caller must be able to fix them all in one pass.

detail.description: e.g. `3 of 134 row(s) would be held; nothing was sent to QuickBooks.`

postable.description: Rows that would have posted — and did not, because of the ones below.

postedIn.description: For `already-posted`: the earlier batch that posted this row.

unknownNames.description: Names this request would send that `qb-lists.json` does not have.

externalId.description: The caller's key. Echoed and stored; never used to decide identity. A v2 save gives a row without one (missing, `null` or `""`) `row-<n>` (1-based position, `-2`, `-3`, ... appended when taken); a v2 edit gives it `edit<v>-<n>`. The original body keeps the bytes as sent.

amount.description: Positive, at most two decimals. The direction comes from `kind`.

account.description: The bank or credit-card account the money moves on.

lineAccount.description: The expense or income account; rules resolve it when it is left out.

last4.description: Last four digits of the account; part of the fingerprint.

post.description: Dashboard v2 §6.1. `false` keeps the row in the request but never sends it: it still counts toward `controlTotal`, and v2 validate and post report it under `skipped` with `reason: "not-to-post"`, never `held`. Missing or `true` means post. Any other value makes the version unreadable in v2 (`$.transactions[i].post: must be true or false`). Every row `false` is refused as `nothing-to-post`.

TxnKind.description: `check` and `deposit` move money on a bank account; `ccCharge` and `ccCredit` on a credit card. Read case-insensitively. `skip` is listed because the serialiser knows it, but it is refused on input (400): to leave a row out of a v2 post, send the row with `post: false`.

PlanRow.description: One submitted row and what would become of it.

requestId.description: First 16 characters of the row's fingerprint.

reason.description: The hold or skip code, e.g. `no-account-rule`, `already-in-quickbooks`, or `not-to-post` for a row marked `post: false` (v2).

batchId.description: The earlier batch this row already posted in.

QbLists.description: The cached QuickBooks names (`qb-lists.json`). Empty lists with a null `syncedUtc` mean the sync has not run.

SavedRequestActor.description: Who did it (§5.3). Users are disabled, never deleted, so an id always has a name.

SavedRequestValidation.description: §6.4. Advisory: Post always validates again. `needsAttention` is set by `unreadable`, `held` and `refused`, not by `unavailable`.

errors.description: Request-level refusals, or the read errors (`$.path: message`).

reason.description: Only when `unavailable`: why validation could not run.

SavedRequestEmailInput.description: Dashboard v2 §5.1: the email this request came from. Every field is optional. A field of the wrong type (or `email` that is not an object) is kept as null; the save still succeeds and nothing is flagged. Never reaches the engine.

receivedUtc.description: An ISO 8601 instant with an offset (`Z` or `+hh:mm`).

SavedRequestEmail.description: Dashboard v2 §5.1: the email read at the v2 save, or `null` when none of the four fields was kept. A field that was missing or malformed is `null`.

SavedRequestSaveBody.description: Dashboard v2 §5: the validate-and-post body, plus the optional `email` and `pushId`. Both are read from the body as received, kept in the original body and version 1, and left out of the canonical hash and change list (§7).

pushId.description: Dashboard v2 §5.2: the sender's id for this push. A UUID is stored and returned lower case with dashes. Anything else is saved, flagged (`$.pushId: not a UUID`, `needsAttention: true`, never cleared) and stays postable. The same `pushId` with the same body answers `200` with the existing record; with a different body `409 push-id-reused`.

PushIdReusedProblem.description: Dashboard v2 §5.2: `push-id-reused`. Names the request that holds the `pushId`.

EditedBySomeoneElseProblem.description: Dashboard v2 §10 4.5: `edited-by-someone-else`. Every v2 `412` (edit, validate, post, discard, restore, resolve) carries the current `rowVersion`, when the request was last changed (`updatedUtc`) and by whom (`updatedBy`).

rowVersion.description: The current row version; send it as `If-Match` after reloading.

updatedUtc.description: When the request was last changed.

updatedBy.description: Who changed it last: a user id or `api-client:<id>`, and the name to show.

SavedRequestSaved.description: §6.1, as served by v2: `needsAttention` and `validation` are the v2 judgement (dashboard v2 §5.3, §6.4), which sets `post: false` rows aside as `not-to-post` and counts a malformed `pushId`.

pushId.description: Lower case with dashes; `null` when none was sent or it was not a UUID.

SavedRequestSummary.description: §6.5: the detail without the payload, the findings and the read errors.

LedgerBatch.description: The ledger batch of an attempt's `postId` (§10.6). Absent when the attempt has no `postId` or the batch cannot be read.

posted.description: The rows QuickBooks accepted, with the transaction ids to look up.

SavedRequestValidationSummary.description: Dashboard v2 §9.1: the v2 snapshot in short.

state.description: The v2 snapshot's state, or `none` when the request has none.

problemCount.description: Findings and errors of the v2 snapshot, plus the metadata errors.

SavedRequestPostSummary.description: Dashboard v2 §9.1: from the latest `posted` or `partial` attempt; for a request settled `posted` by resolve without one, `postedCount` is `null`, `postedUtc` the resolution time and `postedBy` the resolver.

SavedRequestOtherPush.description: Dashboard v2 §9.1: another request with the same non-empty reference that is `pending`, `posting`, `partial` or `unknown`.

receivedUtc.description: The email's `receivedUtc`, else the save time. The list is ordered by it.

SavedRequestLedgerBatch.description: Dashboard v2 §10 4.9: set when the request is `partial` or `unknown`, its last attempt has a `postId`, and the ledger has that batch; otherwise `null`.

SavedRequestSummaryV2.description: Dashboard v2 §9.1: the v1 row (§6.5) with `needsAttention` and `validation` from the v2 judgement, plus `pushId`, `email`, `historyCount`, `validationSummary`, `postSummary` and `skipCount`.

pushId.description: Lower case with dashes; `null` when none was sent at a v2 save or it was not a UUID.

historyCount.description: How many audit events the request has (§8.4).

skipCount.description: Rows of the current version sent with `post: false`.

SavedRequestDetailV2.description: Dashboard v2 §9.1: the v1 detail (§6.2) with `needsAttention`, `validation` (its `versionNumber` is the version judged, §10 4.3) and `readErrors` from the v2 judgement, plus the list row's additions, `otherUnpostedPushes` and `ledgerBatch`.

readErrors.description: The metadata errors first, then the read errors of the current version, then its `post` errors (§6.4).

pushId.description: Lower case with dashes; `null` when none was sent at a v2 save or it was not a UUID.

historyCount.description: How many audit events the request has (§8.4).

skipCount.description: Rows of the current version sent with `post: false`.

LedgerBatchV2.description: The ledger batch of an attempt's `postId` (§10.6). Absent when the attempt has no `postId` or the batch cannot be read.

posted.description: The rows QuickBooks accepted, with the transaction ids to look up.

externalId.description: The `externalId` of the row with this `index` (§10 4.8).

result.description: As stored. After a post, `result.posted[]` lists each row QuickBooks accepted with `index`, `externalId` and `txnId`.

range.description: The request, echoed with `from` and `to` rendered in `tz` with its offset.

previous.description: The compare range's counts; `null` when no compare range was sent.

rows.description: Entries of `posted[]` over the posted and partial attempts that finished in the range.

previousRows.description: As `rows`, for the compare range; `null` without one.

previousAmount.description: As `amount`, for the compare range; `null` without one.

timeToPost.description: `null` when no request has a post time in the range.

start.description: The bucket's local date in `tz` (the Monday for weeks).
